title: Rabbi Kruspedai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Zohar Chadash, Ruth, locator פ״א, where it is related that he fell ill and Rabbi Yose ben Kisma and the Rabbis went in to him. On Shabbat they thought he had died, and afterward, at the close of Shabbat, he revived; see there. In the Zohar, Shelach 164b: he always went up to the Torah as the sixth, and he lived long; see there. Hyman suggests that perhaps there were two people of this name.

notes.text: פ״א remains literal rather than being assigned categorically to folio 81 or chapter 1. Both cited Zohar locations remain unverified, and Hyman’s suggestion that there may be two people remains a conjecture. The notice stays held.

The supplied final expression is ועולי שנים היו; the translation understands ועולי as ואולי, “perhaps,” in Hyman’s suggestion that two people may be involved. The literal supplied letters remain preserved; this is a disclosed contextual reading.

The consulted Zohar Chadash, Midrash Rut 235–250, names Rabbi Yose ben Kisma among the visitors on Shabbat. The visitors realize that Kruspedai is alive when they see tears and a smile. He opens his eyes and asks for water in the evening. The story is indexed under the literal locator פ׳ ע״ב–פ׳ ע״ג in the Zohar Stories edition. Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 851) retains פ״א and ends ואולי שנים היו, “perhaps there were two,” where the supplied transcription has ועולי. The consulted Zohar III, Shelach 164b, has Rabbi Shimon say that Kruspedai only took the sixth reading and describes him as long-lived. Hyman’s suggestion remains tentative.
